subject: VPC deploy: interface contracts and control/data separation
messages:
From: Alex Song <alex.song@acme.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: onpremops@edgecloud.io, procurement@acme.com
Date: Fri, 9 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: VPC deploy: interface contracts and control/data separation

Hi Rishi,

Thanks for the sync earlier. Attaching Acme's current topology (acme_nw_topology_v2.drawio) and a short matrix of existing egress rules (vpc_interface_matrix_v1.pdf). High-level asks from our infra team:

- Confirm where Redwood expects the control-plane endpoints to live (public vs private endpoints).
- If control plane is hosted, what CIDRs/FQDNs need to be allowed for management and health checks?
- For the data plane on-prem, we need a clear list of ports and TLS expectations, plus how KV cache/metrics egress will flow.
- Special compliance ask: we must document cert rotation semantics and proof of encryption-in-transit for audits.

Our target for cutover is the week of Apr 26th; we need a mutual action list by next week. Can you confirm Redwood's acceptance criteria for a canary and what operational runbooks you will require?

Thanks,
Alex Song
Infrastructure Lead, Acme Industries

---

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Song <alex.song@acme.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 9 Apr 2027 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: VPC deploy: interface contracts and control/data separation

Alex — thanks for the artifacts. Quick summary of our proposed stance and what we need from Acme to move forward: 

Proposed topology (short):
- Control plane: Redwood-hosted, public-managed control endpoints with private-link style connectivity where available. We will provide stable FQDNs and a short list of IP ranges for the control plane.
- Data plane: Customer-managed on-prem VPC subnets. Data plane nodes will initiate outbound connections to our control endpoints (TLS 1.2+ with mTLS where required). No inbound SSH or management ports from the public internet to customer nodes.

Network/ops requirements for canary acceptance:
- Allow outbound to control-plane FQDNs on TCP 443. We'll deliver the exact FQDN list by Monday (includes health, telemetry, and model pull endpoints).
- Provide one /28 for our management egress if you prefer IP allowlist; otherwise we will rely on FQDN allowlist + signed certs.
- mTLS for control plane registration and KV sync. We rotate node certs quarterly; please confirm your ops team can accept short-lived client certs.
- Egress behavior: runtime metrics and audit logs will be pushed to our metrics ingestion endpoint (TLS). We can support egress proxying if needed; note that proxying adds 1–2s extra latency.

Compliance and runbooks:
- We will share a draft runbook covering failover, cert rotation, and incident playbooks.
- For SOC2 evidence: we can provide encryption-in-transit statements, cert chain info, and audit log export examples.

Action items (Rishi/Redwood):
1) Deliver control-plane FQDN list and a mapping doc (by 2027-04-12).
2) Draft runbook and canary checklist (by 2027-04-15).
3) Schedule a technical working session for port/CIDR validation (target: week of Apr 12).

Action items (Acme):
A) Confirm whether you prefer FQDN vs IP allowlist for control-plane (reply by Tue 2027-04-13).
B) Share egress/proxy constraints and an expected maintenance blackout window (by Tue).

I'll also drop our reference wiring diagram into Drive.

— Rishi Malhotra
Senior Product Manager, Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai

---

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alex Song <alex.song@acme.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 10 Apr 2027 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: VPC deploy: interface contracts and control/data separation

Thanks Rishi/Alex — a couple of clarifying points from the networking side: 

1) Cert rotation model: we prefer the short-lived client certs approach (30d). Can Acme accept a client cert rotation API or will you require manual import? If manual, we need an audit path documented.
2) Ports: for data-plane control and KV sync we will need outbound TCP 443, and a small set of high ports for model content prefetch (we can restrict to 10240-10300 if you need).
3) CIDR size: if you go IP allowlist, a /28 is tight but manageable — please confirm public IP stability for the egress box.

Irene
Network Engineer, Redwood Inference

---

From: Alex Song <alex.song@acme.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: onpremops@edgecloud.io, procurement@acme.com
Date: Sat, 10 Apr 2027 11:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: VPC deploy: interface contracts and control/data separation

Rishi/Irene — we prefer FQDN allowlist but can provision a /28 if Redwood needs strict IP allowlisting. Attached is our minimal egress inventory (partial) and a list of maintenance windows for April. We can support a 2-hour on-site cutover slot on Apr 27th or Apr 29th.

Cert rotation: we can accept a cert rotation endpoint if you provide a short integration doc. We've also uploaded our SOC excerpts to the shared Drive folder.

I'll coordinate with procurement on the MSA changes (cc'd).

Cheers,
Alex

---

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Song <alex.song@acme.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 11 Apr 2027 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: VPC deploy: interface contracts and control/data separation

Appreciate the quick turnaround, everyone. A few logistical notes and next steps: 

- Rishi: please publish the FQDN list and the draft runbook to the Drive link referenced in the thread by Monday so Acme's team can confirm.
- Jonas: please open the JIRA ticket SUP-1249 for the on-prem cutover run and link the canary checklist.
- Alex: confirm Apr 27th as the preferred canary window. We'll treat Apr 29th as backup.
- Procurement: if MSA redlines are bundled, please flag anything that affects network isolation or audit requirements.

We aim for a limited canary with a single tenant and rollback plan that includes immediate unbinding of the node and a 15-minute failback. Rishi, include the rollback steps in the runbook.

Thanks — Kim
Kimberly Park
VP, Product Operations, Redwood Inference
